newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen $1 down, Brent flat to 5 cts up.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen $1 down, Brent flat to 5 cts up.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were called to open $1 a tonne lower on Thursday while Brent futures were called unchanged to five cents higher, brokers said.
Gas oil was expected to catch up with Brent's late losses on Wednesday, when the June contract shed 33 cents to close near session lows at $17.81 a barrel.
May gas oil closed $2.75 a tonne lower at $162.50.
"We're looking for $1 down on the gas oil, that's for sure," said a broker.
Brokers said sentiment remained soft after Wednesday's heavy losses prompted by rising U.S. stocks and weak gasoline demand.

Industry and government data showed U.S. stocks of crude, middle distillates and gasoline all rose last week and the American Petroleum Institute said on Wednesday gasoline supply should more than match peak driving season demand this summer.
Both Brent and gas oil fell on Wednesday as some fund selling set into the market, one broker added.
June Brent on SIMEX traded three cents firmer at $17.84 a barrel by 0820 GMT.
Some brokers said gas oil remained well supported in Europe after recent shipments to the Far East. Wednesday's close above support at $162 a tonne was also encouraging, they said.

News of a gas leak overnight at Tosco Corp's 104,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery in Rodeo, California, which forced the company to scale back throughput at some units, could provide mild support, brokers said.
But the technical picture for Brent remained weak, with any break through $17.80 a barrel signalling a move towards $17.47, analysts said.
